name: Ranthambore & Rajasthan
about: The tiger reserve closes entirely Jul–Sep for monsoon. Apr–Jun is brutally hot but gives the best tiger sightings as vegetation thins.
overview: One of India's best places to see a wild tiger, set among the ruins of a 10th-century fort inside the reserve, with the real cities and palaces of Rajasthan a short trip away.
costOverview: Ranthambore and Rajasthan stay cheap even with a tiger safari built in — a full thali dinner costs just a few dollars, and the safari itself, the main reason most visitors come, remains affordable by international standards.

specialSeasons.text: Thinning vegetation as the dry season peaks makes this the best window for tiger sightings.
